column1: # Spark — freshness, invalidation and conflict contract for operative facts (contract version 1)
# This file is the machine-readable authority for how an operative fact (preferences/fact-model.tsv,
# schema version 1) becomes stale, what a consumer does when a source cannot be re-read, and how
# conflicting evidence resolves. reference/fact-freshness.md renders the same records for a reader and
# is checked against this data by the behavioral suite tests/test-fact-freshness.sh; prose is never
# Record kinds (tab-separated; a line starting with # is a comment):
#   schema      <n>                                      the fact-model schema version it is written against
#   event       <name> <fires> <observed-as> <meaning>   an invalidation event class; fires = invalidator kinds (or none)
#   kinds       <class> <invalidator kinds> <why>        the tokens a class's facts may carry (inputs = the union of a derived fact's inputs)
#   effect      <token> <meaning>                        the closed vocabulary of the matrix cells
#   matrix      <class> <effect per event, in event order, comma-separated>   derived from kinds × fires (F2); the suite recomputes it
#   conflict    <situation> <outcome> <detail> <rule>    deterministic outcome for conflicting or duplicate evidence
#   unreadable  <failure> <status> <reason-form> <rule>  status when a source cannot be re-read
#   depends     <class> <events> <why>                 the events that can change the class's value; each must reach it in the matrix (F12)
#   scenario    <name> <event> <fired token> <stale;re-read;derived> <note>   executable: applied to Example 1 of the fact model
#   rule        <id> <statement>                         the rules a consumer must honor, verbatim on the page
# --- Events: what changes, which invalidator kinds fire, how a consumer observes it

column4: the pull request's head commit differs from the head: token
column5: A pull request's HEAD moves — a new commit, a rebase or a force-push. Every fact carrying head:<old> is stale; nothing judged on the old HEAD is reused for the new one.

column4: the base branch's target commit differs from the head fact's base
column5: The base branch the work unit targets moves. Facts carrying ref:<repository>/<base_ref> are stale: the head fact's base commit and the merge picture change while the HEAD stands.

column4: the node's updated_at is later than the fact's source.version, or the node is closed, reopened, transferred or deleted
column5: An issue's or pull request's title, body, state, labels, assignees, milestone or native relationships change. Facts carrying issue:/pull_request:<that node> are stale.

column4: the comment's updated_at is later than the fact's source.version, or the comment is gone; for a created comment, its node's updated_at moves
column5: A comment that records a verdict or a decision is created, edited or deleted. An edit or deletion fires comment:<that comment>; a creation cannot fire a token no fact carries yet, so it fires the node's own token — a fact whose value depends on which records a node carries lists that node (fact model R17).

column4: a parent, child, blocker or milestone listed by the fact changes state or membership
column5: A parent, child, blocker or milestone relationship changes. The graph and placement facts that list the related node or the milestone are stale.

column4: the check-runs listing for the HEAD (latest per name) differs from results, or any result is non-terminal
column5: A check run or workflow run at the HEAD completes, is re-run or is requested. No token changes — the HEAD is the same — so the checks fact is re-read on observation: a non-terminal result is never carried forward and a terminal one is re-read when a merge decision is derived.

column4: the repository's rulesets or the required-check set differ from required
column5: The repository's rulesets change which checks are required. The checks fact for every open work unit carries ruleset:<repository> and is stale.

column4: the repository's updated_at, default branch, settings or the observing identity's permission differ from what was read
column5: Repository settings, the default branch or the observing identity's permission change. Facts carrying repository:<repository> are stale, and every other source-read fact of the set is re-read (F13): readability was a property of the snapshot, and after a permission loss each re-read yields UNKNOWN (unreadable records).

column4: the snapshot's schema_version differs from the consumer's fact-model version, or the compiler that derived a fact changed its version
column5: The fact model's schema version or the compiler's interpretation changes. Every fact of the snapshot is UNKNOWN to that consumer (R9); the snapshot is recompiled, never migrated in place.

column4: a read of the source fails: permission denied, not found, rate-limited, timed out, or malformed
column5: An authoritative source cannot be re-read. The fact takes the status the unreadable record assigns, with detail.reason naming the failure; the previous value is never reused as authority.

the HEAD moves, a check runs or re-runs at the HEAD, or the required set changes

column1: # --- Effects: the closed vocabulary of the class × event matrix

column3: an event fires a token the fact carries: the fact is not usable until re-read from its source

no token of the fact fires, but the source can have changed at the same identity (a check run at the HEAD) or the set's readability has changed (a repository event, F13): the fact is re-read before it is used
an input of the derived fact is stale or re-read: the fact is re-derived from re-read inputs (R4, R15), never patched
the fact is UNKNOWN to the consumer until the source is re-read or the snapshot recompiled (R9, unreadable records)
the event cannot change the fact: no token it carries fires

column1: # --- Matrix: derived — for each class, the effect of each event in event order (F2)
# --- Conflicts: deterministic outcomes (R8); a human or a released contract resolves a CONFLICT, never the model

column4: reason names the disagreement; candidates list every record's identity
column5: Two authoritative inputs disagree (two trusted verdict records for one HEAD, two decision records for one grant): CONFLICT with both named; no first-write, last-write or plausibility rule chooses (R8).

column4: reason names the malformation; candidates list the malformed and the valid record
column5: A record that does not parse or does not canonicalize stands beside a valid one for the same fact: CONFLICT, because the model cannot know which the author meant (status CONFLICT).

column4: no detail; source.identity is the earliest record; every duplicate is listed as an invalidator
column5: Two or more records for one fact say the same thing: ESTABLISHED from the earliest durable record, every duplicate carried as a comment: token so an edit to any of them fires.

column4: no detail; the fact carries the canonical spelling
column5: A source spells an identity in a projection (upper-case owner, refs/heads/ prefix, .git suffix, a bare issue number): the compiler emits the one canonical representation (R1); a record whose identity does not canonicalize to one representation is malformed evidence.

column4: no fact of the current snapshot; the record stays reachable through provenance
column5: Evidence judged on another HEAD (a PASS for head:A when the HEAD is B) is historical: its head: token names the other HEAD, it never enters the current fact and it never conflicts with current evidence (Example 3 of the fact model).

column4: alone: UNKNOWN with the record in candidates; beside a valid record: CONFLICT
column5: A record that carries the same field twice (two id fields, two status fields) is malformed before parsing, whatever the values: alone it follows the malformed-alone unreadable record, beside a valid record the malformed-beside-valid conflict record. A consumer that keeps the first or the last duplicate is not conforming (fact model R14).

column4: no fact of the current snapshot; the record stays reachable through provenance
column5: Evidence that belongs to another work unit (a grant targeting another repository, a review on another pull request) is historical for this snapshot: it is distinguishable by its work-unit token and confers nothing here (Example 6 of the fact model).

column1: # --- Unreadable sources: the status a failed re-read yields; the old value is never authority again

column4: HTTP 401 or 403 for the observing identity, with the endpoint
column5: The observing identity may not read the source: UNKNOWN, never a permissive default and never the previous value (Example 7 of the fact model).

column4: HTTP 404 with the node or record identity
column5: The node or record is gone, transferred or never existed: UNKNOWN; a decision or verdict whose record is gone confers nothing.

column4: HTTP 429, or 403 with a rate-limit header, with the reset time
column5: The source refused the read for now: UNKNOWN until a later read; the consumer schedules the retry, the fact does not pretend.

column4: the transport error, with the endpoint
column5: The read did not complete: UNKNOWN; a partial response is no response.

column4: the parse or canonicalization failure, with the record identity in candidates
column5: The only record for a fact does not parse or does not canonicalize: UNKNOWN with the record named, so an auditor can drill down; beside a valid record it is a CONFLICT instead.

column1: # --- Migration: schema and compiler version changes

column4: A consumer at fact-model schema version 1 reads only snapshots with schema_version 1. Any other version makes every fact UNKNOWN to it (R9). Nothing is migrated in place: a snapshot is recompiled by a compiler of the consumer's version. Once a version has shipped in a Spark release, a compiler change that alters how a fact is interpreted is a new schema version, so the version string of every derived fact changes with it (R4); until it ships, the version is corrected in place and the release that ships it fixes it (fact model R19).

column4: repository:github.com/acme/widgets

column6: The observing identity loses read access (a repository event): the repository fact is stale and, under F13, every other source-read fact is re-read before use; each re-read answers 403 and yields UNKNOWN (Example 7 of the fact model), so nothing cached stays authoritative.

column3: Freshness is decided by identity, never by age. A fact is current while every token it carries names an unchanged node and its source.version is the source's current version; a time-based check may trigger a re-read but never keeps a fact current.

An event fires the invalidator kinds its event record lists. A fact is stale exactly when an event fires a token it carries; the class × event matrix is derived from the class kinds and the event kinds and is never edited by hand.

A stale fact is not usable as authority. It is re-read from its source, and the re-read yields ESTABLISHED, UNKNOWN, CONFLICT or NOT_APPLICABLE per the fact model; the previous value survives only as provenance.
A derived fact is re-derived whenever any input is stale or re-read (R4, R15); it is never patched, and its version string changes with any input's version.

A source that cannot be re-read yields the status its unreadable record assigns, with detail.reason naming the failure and detail.candidates naming what could be seen. The old value never survives as authority: there is no stale authoritative reuse.
Conflicts resolve only by the conflict records: both candidates named, no first-write, no last-write, no plausibility (R8). A released contract may add a precedence rule; the model never infers one.
Evidence for another HEAD or another work unit is historical, distinguishable by its head: or work-unit token; it never enters the current fact and never competes with current evidence.
A schema or compiler version mismatch makes every fact UNKNOWN to the consumer (R9). There is no in-place migration in this version; a snapshot is recompiled.
Provenance is a pointer (R2, R3, R16). Deciding freshness reads tokens and versions in the snapshot, never history; drill-down loads the source on demand.

Checks are observation-fresh at a HEAD: a non-terminal result is never carried into a snapshot that decides an action, and a terminal result is re-read when a merge decision is derived, because a check can be re-run at the same HEAD without any token changing.
Cached or inferred capability never becomes authority (R5). An authority fact changes only through its decision records; a permission change makes reads UNKNOWN, it grants nothing.

Readability is a property of the snapshot. Every source-read fact of a set was read by one observing identity under the set's repository's permissions, and every such fact belongs to that repository (R17). A repository event — settings, default branch or the observing identity's permission — makes the repository fact stale and re-reads every other source-read fact of the set, so a permission loss cannot leave a cached fact usable: the re-read yields UNKNOWN through the unreadable records.

Every event that can change a fact's value reaches the fact through a token it carries: the depends record of each class names those events, and the matrix cell for each is stale or re-read (derived for the derived class). A fact whose value depends on which records a node carries lists the node itself, so a record created after the fact was read fires a token the fact already has.
